subject: Performance / SLO follow-up: concurrency, latency, and Redwood rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@nimbus.ai>, Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance call recap — concurrency + rate limits (Nimbus)

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciate the walkthrough of your prod traffic patterns. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we have alignment before I pull the capacity/engineering teams in.

Summary of asks we discussed:
- Latency SLO: P95 <= 600ms for streaming chat responses (end-to-end token generation).
- Throughput: average 200 reqs/min with 10x peak bursts (2,000 reqs/min) for launches.
- Concurrency: 350 concurrent open connections for streaming sessions; up to 1,200 parallel non-streaming (batch) inference requests during peak ETL windows.
- Connection pooling: you mentioned using a pool of long-lived connections from your edge -> Redwood; recommended keepalive and 500 connection pool per pool IP.
- Retry/backoff tolerance: graceful 429 handling and ability to accept spike-burst fallbacks to a lower-capacity model variant.

Requested from you (if you can share):
- Spreadsheet of hourly peak/day-of-week (we discussed a sample) — will help sizing.
- Any hard constraints on connection reuse or pinned TLS session requirements.

Attachments: I attached a short template XLS for concurrency/traffic (#1). Please fill out rows for typical/peak/launch.

Next steps:
1) Alex to send requested traffic sheet by end of day Friday.
2) Redwood to produce an initial rate-limit/quota proposal and a pilot config (canary) for the first 30 days.
3) Technical kickoff w/ infra & capacity (proposed week of Jun 14).

If anything above needs correction, flag it in reply and I’ll update the mutual action plan.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: nimbus-concurrency-reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet template)

From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@nimbus.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance call recap — concurrency + rate limits (Nimbus)

Thanks Marissa — big help. Filling out the sheet now; attaching a high-level traffic export and answers inline below.

Inline answers:
- Confirm P95 target: 600ms (we can tolerate P99 up to 1.2s for long-tail).
- Throughput: baseline 180–220 reqs/min; peak hourly bursts ~2,200/min during product launches.
- Concurrency detail: 320–380 concurrent streaming sessions typical (concurrent open WS/HTTP-streams). Non-streaming parallel inference: ~900 sustained during ETL (30 min windows), short spikes to 1,250 for <10 minutes.
- Connection pooling: we use 4 outbound egress IPs per AZ; each service instance keeps ~250 persistent connections. We can add more pool IPs but prefer to keep under 8 IPs total.
- Retry/backoff: standard exponential backoff; prefer 429 retries up to 3 with jitter.

Attached: nimbus-traffic-export.csv (hourly), completed nimbus-concurrency-reqs.xlsx

Let us know what you recommend for a pilot quota and what shape rate-limits will take (per-IP, per-API-key, per-connection?). We have a procurement checkpoint next Tue and would like a pilot quote to share.

—
Alex Thompson
Engineering Manager, Nimbus AI
alex.thompson@nimbus.ai
Attachment: nimbus-concurrency-reqs.xlsx, nimbus-traffic-export.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance call recap — concurrency + rate limits (Nimbus)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alex — the sheet looks great and the hourly export helped a ton. Based on your numbers I pulled an initial proposal from Capacity for a pilot configuration and a draft of how Redwood rate limits would be expressed: see attached redwood-rate-limits-draft.pdf and the attached mutual-action-plan-nimbus.docx. Highlights below.

Pilot proposal (30 days):
- Dedicated reserved pool (pilot tier): enough vGPU capacity to sustain 900 parallel non-streaming requests and 400 concurrent streaming sessions with burst headroom to 1,400 non-streaming requests for short spikes.
- Rate limits: default enforcement at API-key level with soft limits per 60s window (recommended for your environment) and optional per-eIP limits we can enable if you provide egress IPs. Example: API-key base quota 1,000 reqs/min, burst allowance to 2,500 reqs/min for 2-minute windows; streaming concurrency cap of 500 per API-key; connection-limit advisory: 500 persistent connections per pool IP.
- Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to a quantized model variant when the pilot pool exceeds 85% sustained utilization; 429 + Retry-After header behavior documented.
- Pricing: pilot monthly commit + overage TPS pricing to be included in HubSpot quote (HubSpot: 67890).

Open items we should confirm before procurement meeting:
- Whether you want per-eIP enforcement (we can restrict by IP, but that requires you to lock down egress or provide a small list).
- TLS session pinning — you indicated no strict requirement; confirm if that changes.
- Canary SLA for production rollout after pilot (proposed 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool).

Next steps:
- I’ll update the mutual action plan with the above and add a timeline for pilot activation (2–3 business days after signed pilot).
- Laura, can you help with a short note on SLA exceptions / enterprise support add-ons so Alex has visibility for procurement?

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood-rate-limits-draft.pdf; mutual-action-plan-nimbus.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance call recap — concurrency + rate limits (Nimbus)

Hi Alex — quick note from ops/enterprise support perspective.

We can support per-eIP enforcement for the pilot but will need your team to supply the static egress IPs and a point of contact for firewall whitelisting. If pinning is off the table, we will rely on API-key + TLS + mTLS options (mTLS available on Private deployments).

SLA & support add-ons:
- Pilot: standard support (business hours) + proactive monitoring included.
- Production Dedicated: can add 24x7 enterprise support + 15 min paging for critical incidents.
- SLA exceptions: can be negotiated for launch windows; will require a short RCF (risk & compliance) review.

Marissa — I’ll add these bullets to the MAP and the draft contract. Alex — if procurement needs a one-pager for internal signoff, I can put together a concise summary of pilot limits and the fallback behavior.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0177

Attachment: none
